Header: Agrotis ipsilon Amharic: gund korach; Tigrigna: gundi koratsi

Prevention: Avoid planting in fields with known history of cutworm problems
Remove wild plants and weeds in the field to prevent cutworm transfering into the next season
Carry out the following sanitation methods:
Deep plough after harvest and during the whole off-season to expose cutworms to the sun and their natural enemies
Weed grasses two weeks before planting
Clean farm land and farm edges before planting
Monitoring: Regularly monitor for the presence of cutworms (on weeds & grasses in the field during the dry season)
Look for the eggs of the cutworm adult moth, these are a whitish yellow colour and found on leaves
The larvae are dark brown/black caterpillars measuring up to 4-5cm.
Look for plants/seedlings that have been cut in rows by the larvae.
Look at the base of the plant or under the soil - dig in the soil to confirm their presence
When the soil is moist, the cutworm caterpillars cut the plant just above the soil surface.
When soil is dry, cutworms will feed on the plant just below the soil surface causing the plant to wilt and die
Direct Control: Hand pick adults early in the morning and crush, bury or put in hot water to kill
Dig around the plant up to the depth of 5cm to expose larvae to predators such as birds and ants
Flood the field with rain water by constructing trenches around the field to drown the pest
Restrictions: There are no registered insecticides in
Ethiopia for the management of cutworm on pepper
